data.title: Shift Cypher
data.statement:
A shift cypher is a simple way of encrypting a message so that it is unreadble at first glance. It works by assigning every letter in the alphabet to another corresponding letter, determined by an integer value key, which is used to uniformly shift the message that many places back or ahead in the alphabet. 

Given the key value and an encoded message, shift the encoded message back to its original, readable state.

Note: only alphabetic characters are shifted. Spaces, punctuation, and numbers remain unchanged, and the original capitalization is preserved.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A shift cypher is a simple way of encrypting a message so that it is unreadble at first glance. It works by assigning every letter in the alphabet to another corresponding letter, determined by an integer value key, which is used to uniformly shift the message that many places back or ahead in the alphabet.

Given the key value and an encoded message, shift the encoded message back to its original, readable state.

Note: only alphabetic characters are shifted. Spaces, punctuation, and numbers remain unchanged, and the original capitalization is preserved.
Input
One line that contains a the encrypted message as a string, m.
A second line that contains the integer value for the number of letters by which the message has been shifted, n.
Output
A string that contains the original, decoded message.
Constraints
Example
Input
Lellvoqew
10
Output
Bubblegum
